**19 commits are on staging but not yet on main.** All of them are already pushed to staging, so nothing local is waiting there.

**New features (13)**
1. WhatsApp messages for order confirmed, rescheduled, delivered and farmer-cancel

4. Farmers can order their own produce

12. Moderator Order Report, for one farmer or all farmers
13. Aggregator's WhatsApp order-placed message names the grower

**Fixes (2)**
- A wrong handover code no longer logs the farmer out
- Supabase images are served unoptimized (this is the Vercel image-overage fix)

**Speed and cost (4)**
- Fewer Vercel function runs and less bandwidth
- Shared produce links open in one round trip
- Home grid loads 15 cards at a time
- Functions run in Mumbai (bom1), next to the database

**Before you merge to main (you asked me to remind you):**

- Most of these have not been tested on a phone yet.

The method is called **cherry-picking**: start from main, then copy over only the commits you want, one at a time.

```bash
git fetch origin
```

I listed every staging commit that main didn't have:
```bash
git rev-list --reverse --no-merges origin/main..origin/staging
```

Then for each commit I ran:

```bash
git cherry-pick -x <commit>
```

`cherry-pick` copies that one commit onto the new branch. `-x` adds a note "(cherry picked from commit …)" so you can trace it back to staging.

There is **no separate payments table**. Payment details are stored on each order in the **`orders`** table, in these columns:

| Column | What it holds |
|---|---|
| `payment_status` | `pending`, `paid`, `completed`, `failed`, `deposit_paid`, `payment_claimed`, `pending_confirmation` |
| `payment_method` | `cod`, `upi`, online, … |
| `total_price` | amount of the order |
| `cashfree_payment_id` / `razorpay_payment_id` | gateway payment ID (online payments only) |
| `refund_status`, `refund_amount` | refunds |

A **successful payment** is `payment_status` = `paid` or `completed`. Both mean money received; the code treats them the same.

```sql
ORDER BY orders DESC;
```

```sql

FROM orders
WHERE payment_status IN ('paid', 'completed');
```

**3. Successful payments split by method** (online vs COD vs UPI)
```sql

FROM orders
WHERE payment_status IN ('paid', 'completed')
GROUP BY payment_method;
```

```sql

FROM orders
WHERE payment_status IN ('paid', 'completed');
```

-- ================================================================
-- YFF Payments: one place to see every payment and its status
-- Run in: Supabase Dashboard → SQL Editor → New Query → Run
-- ================================================================
--
-- There is no payments table: payment details live on each `orders` row
-- (payment_status, payment_method, gateway ids, refund columns), and every
-- payment_status change is already logged in `order_events`
-- (event_type = 'payment_change'). These are VIEWS over `orders`, not copies,
-- so they can never drift out of sync and need no trigger.
--
--   payments                -- one row per order, payment columns only
--   payment_status_summary  -- count + amount per payment_status
--
-- "Successful" = payment_status 'paid' or 'completed' (the code treats the
-- two the same). A multi-farmer checkout is ONE payment but several order
-- rows; `payment_ref` groups them, so COUNT(DISTINCT payment_ref) counts
-- real payments.
--
-- Not readable from the app: security_invoker makes the view obey the caller's
-- rights on `orders`, and anon/authenticated get no grant at all. Read it from
-- the SQL Editor or the Table Editor (service role).
--
-- Safe to re-run.

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW public.payments
WITH (security_invoker = true) AS
SELECT
  o.id                                    AS order_id,
  o.order_code,
  COALESCE(o.checkout_id, o.id)           AS payment_ref,
  o.created_at,
  o.buyer_name,
  o.buyer_phone,
  o.farmer_id,
  o.produce_name,
  o.total_price,
  o.delivery_fee,
  o.platform_fee,
  o.payment_method,
  o.payment_method_detail,
  o.payment_status,
  o.payment_status IN ('paid', 'completed') AS is_successful,
  o.paid_at,
  COALESCE(o.cashfree_order_id, o.razorpay_order_id)     AS gateway_order_id,
  COALESCE(o.cashfree_payment_id, o.razorpay_payment_id) AS gateway_payment_id,
  CASE
    WHEN o.cashfree_order_id IS NOT NULL THEN 'cashfree'
    WHEN o.razorpay_order_id IS NOT NULL THEN 'razorpay'
  END                                     AS gateway,
  o.utr_number,
  o.cod_deposit,
  o.cod_balance_due,
  o.cod_deposit_paid_at,
  o.cash_collected_at,
  o.refund_status,
  o.refund_amount,
  o.refunded_at,
  o.status                                AS order_status
FROM public.orders o;

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW public.payment_status_summary
WITH (security_invoker = true) AS
SELECT
  payment_status,
  COUNT(*)                    AS orders,
  COUNT(DISTINCT payment_ref) AS payments,
  SUM(total_price)            AS amount
FROM public.payments
GROUP BY payment_status;

-- ================================================================
-- YFF Payments: one place to see every payment and its status
-- Run in: Supabase Dashboard → SQL Editor → New Query → Run
-- ================================================================
--
-- There is no payments table: payment details live on each `orders` row
-- (payment_status, payment_method, gateway ids, refund columns), and every
-- payment_status change is already logged in `order_events`
-- (event_type = 'payment_change'). These are VIEWS over `orders`, not copies,
-- so they can never drift out of sync and need no trigger.
--
--   payments                -- one row per order: buyer, farmer, amounts, status
--   payment_status_summary  -- count + amount per payment_status
--
-- Reading the numbers:
--   • is_successful = payment_status 'paid' or 'completed' (the code treats the
--     two the same).
--   • A refund does NOT change payment_status — the order stays 'paid' and only
--     refund_status/refund_amount are set. net_received subtracts the refund.
--   • verified_by: 'gateway' = Cashfree/Razorpay confirmed the money;
--     'farmer' = a COD/UPI order the farmer (or rider) marked as paid.
--   • buyer_paid = produce + delivery fee + platform fee (same sum as
--     src/lib/orderReport.ts). total_price alone is the produce price.
--   • A multi-farmer checkout is ONE payment but several order rows;
--     COUNT(DISTINCT payment_ref) counts real payments.
--
-- Not readable from the app: security_invoker makes the view obey the caller's
-- rights on `orders`, and anon/authenticated get no grant at all. Read it from
-- the SQL Editor or the Table Editor (service role).
--
-- Safe to re-run (dropped and recreated — views hold no data).

DROP VIEW IF EXISTS public.payment_status_summary;
DROP VIEW IF EXISTS public.payments;

CREATE VIEW public.payments
WITH (security_invoker = true) AS
SELECT
  o.id                                    AS order_id,
  o.order_code,
  COALESCE(o.checkout_id, o.id)           AS payment_ref,
  o.created_at,
  -- who paid
  o.buyer_name,
  o.buyer_phone,
  -- who was paid
  f.name                                  AS farmer_name,
  f.phone                                 AS farmer_phone,
  f.village                               AS farmer_village,
  f.account_type                          AS farmer_account_type,
  o.is_self_order,
  -- what and how much
  o.produce_name,
  o.quantity,
  o.unit,
  o.total_price                           AS produce_amount,
  o.delivery_fee,
  o.platform_fee,
  COALESCE(o.total_price, 0) + COALESCE(o.delivery_fee, 0) + COALESCE(o.platform_fee, 0)
                                          AS buyer_paid,
  COALESCE(o.refund_amount, 0)            AS refund_amount,
  CASE WHEN o.payment_status IN ('paid', 'completed')
    THEN COALESCE(o.total_price, 0) + COALESCE(o.delivery_fee, 0) + COALESCE(o.platform_fee, 0)
         - COALESCE(o.refund_amount, 0)
    ELSE 0
  END                                     AS net_received,
  -- status
  o.payment_method,
  o.payment_method_detail,
  o.payment_status,
  o.payment_status IN ('paid', 'completed') AS is_successful,
  CASE
    WHEN o.payment_status NOT IN ('paid', 'completed', 'deposit_paid') THEN NULL
    WHEN COALESCE(o.cashfree_payment_id, o.razorpay_payment_id) IS NOT NULL THEN 'gateway'
    ELSE 'farmer'
  END                                     AS verified_by,
  o.paid_at,
  CASE
    WHEN o.cashfree_order_id IS NOT NULL THEN 'cashfree'
    WHEN o.razorpay_order_id IS NOT NULL THEN 'razorpay'
  END                                     AS gateway,
  COALESCE(o.cashfree_order_id, o.razorpay_order_id)     AS gateway_order_id,
  COALESCE(o.cashfree_payment_id, o.razorpay_payment_id) AS gateway_payment_id,
  o.utr_number,
  o.cod_deposit,
  o.cod_balance_due,
  o.cod_deposit_paid_at,
  o.cash_collected_at,
  o.refund_status,
  o.refunded_at,
  o.status                                AS order_status
FROM public.orders o
LEFT JOIN public.farmers f ON f.id = o.farmer_id;

CREATE VIEW public.payment_status_summary
WITH (security_invoker = true) AS
SELECT
  payment_status,
  COUNT(*)                    AS orders,
  COUNT(DISTINCT payment_ref) AS payments,
  SUM(buyer_paid)             AS buyer_paid,
  SUM(refund_amount)          AS refunded,
  SUM(net_received)           AS net_received
FROM public.payments
GROUP BY payment_status;

REVOKE ALL ON public.payments, public.payment_status_summary FROM anon, authenticated;

I can't say yet whether 33,000 is real, because I can't see your data. Most likely it's **too high**: the first version of the table counted every `paid` and `completed` order as money received, even when it shouldn't.

**What could be inflating it:**
1. **Refunds were still counted.** When an order is refunded it stays `paid`; only `refund_amount` is filled in. So refunded money was still in the total.
